title: Why I Finally Switched to Cycling to Work
script: Narrator: [reflective] For years, I dismissed cycling to work as impractical, even though several colleagues had been quietly doing it the whole time.
Narrator: [honest] My excuses were always the same: the distance, the traffic, and, frankly, my own laziness on cold mornings.
Narrator: [thoughtful] What actually changed my mind wasn't a health scare or advice from a doctor, but a single ridiculous traffic jam.
Narrator: [amused] I sat in my car for fifty minutes to cover a distance I could have walked in under an hour.
Narrator: [determined] That evening, I looked up the cycling route properly, and it turned out to be barely twenty minutes if the roads were clear.
Narrator: [honest] I still hesitated for another two weeks, mostly because I dreaded arriving at the office looking sweaty and disheveled.
Narrator: [practical] Eventually, I solved that by packing a change of shirt, which sounds obvious now but hadn't occurred to me at all.
Narrator: [reflective] The first ride was harder than expected, and as a result, I arrived slightly late and thoroughly out of breath.
Narrator: [warmly] Even so, something about that ride felt different, less like a chore and more like a small daily achievement.
Narrator: [thoughtful] Within a month, my fitness improved noticeably, even though improving fitness had never actually been my original goal.
Narrator: [honest] What surprised me most was the mental clarity, arriving at work already awake instead of groggy from sitting in traffic.
Narrator: [practical] Financially, it made a real difference too, since fuel and parking costs had quietly been draining my monthly budget.
Narrator: [reflective] Despite the occasional rainy morning, which admittedly I still dread, I haven't gone back to driving regularly since.
Narrator: [warmly] My colleagues who cycle now nod at me differently, as if I've finally joined some unspoken, slightly smug club.
Narrator: [encouraging] If a single traffic jam could change my mind after years of excuses, maybe your excuses aren't as solid as they feel either.
